newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products turn narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products turn narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices turned narrowly mixed on late Wednesday, with a dearth of traders leaving the market directionless.
And NYMEX November futures failed to provide momentum, as gasoline fell 0.40 cent to 62.42 cents a gallon and crude rose a mere nine to $24.05 a barrel.
Values dropped after weekly inventory reports from industry and government showed growing gasoline supply.
Data from the trade group American Petroleum Institute showed stocks nationwide rose 2.27 million last week to 197.1 million barrels.
Early Wednesday, the U.S. Energy Information Administration, released its weekly inventory report which showed gasoline in storage climbed 4.2 million barrels to 197.7 million barrels.
And traders also said PADD 5 would lose demand from the Pacific Northwest, where cooler weather slows driving demand.
Bids for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles rose half a cent to 65 cents a gallon, while offers remained 66.00 cents a gallon.
Conventional grade gasoline in L.A. added a half cent fall to early declines and ended 70/71 cents a gallon.
San Francisco grades tracked L.A. at a steady 1.50-cent discount.
Among distillates, CARB diesel held strong at 80/81 cents a gallon, after refiners cut back production last month to process better-priced jet fuel.
